question: Is the off-source midpoint observed in Experiment 004 already present when the continuous interpolated state is independently projected to vocabulary tokens, or is it created during diffusion denoising?

design.projection_repeat_reason: Highest-scoring vocabulary projection is deterministic and does not sample.
design.mixing: Global arithmetic interpolation of corresponding final prompt-conditioned canvas-state positions.

measurements: Global and position-wise parent cosine similarity.
Exact projected token IDs and decoded zero-step text at every weight.
Per-position projected-token agreement with each endpoint.
Hash-verified references to all Experiment 004 eight-step controls.

interpretation.off_source_at_projection: If the midpoint has already lost both techniques at zero steps, independent vocabulary projection is an early information bottleneck.
interpretation.source_information_before_denoising: If zero-step text or tokens retain both techniques but eight-step outputs do not, later denoising causes the collapse.
interpretation.geometric_cancellation: Very low midpoint norm or opposing parent directions would support destructive vector cancellation.
interpretation.no_geometric_cancellation: A normal midpoint norm with positive parent cosine would rule out simple cancellation and implicate nonlinear projection or model decoding.

important_limitations: This diagnoses final prompt-conditioned canvas states only.
Decoded zero-step text is an imperfect view of token-level information, so token IDs and endpoint overlap are also retained.
Experiment 004 controls are reused rather than rerun to avoid unnecessary GPU cost.
This remains exploratory evidence from one prompt pair and one model revision.
